clue.text: Reprimanding two females after revealing nothing

indicators.note: after says the two females come behind the other pieces

parts.note: revealing a secret is telling it
O looks like zero, nothing
F is the standard abbreviation for female, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: A scolding delivered once a pair of women give nothing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding or reprimand is the British idiom for a dressing-down given to someone, so the phrase works as a noun-like gerund.

clue.text: Heading for opera, papa wears such?

definitions.text: Heading for opera, papa wears such?

indicators.note: the word for such wears the other letters, holding them inside it like a garment

parts.note: such means that, as in 'that kind of thing'

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of opera is used

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Dad heading off to the opera dresses in formal headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' puts OP inside THAT. As a whole the clue also describes the tall formal hat a father might put on for a night at the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall silk hat is traditional formal evening wear, the sort of thing worn to the opera.

clue.text: Left behind schedule after parking — sign of a new driver

indicators.note: after puts the late part following the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign symbol for parking
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: A learner left in a car park, running late.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver must display a red L on a white plate on the car.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-lettered plate marks a car driven by a learner, so it signals someone new to driving.

clue.text: Decreasing surface?

parts.note: read decreasing as de-creasing: a surface on which creases are taken out of clothes

explanation.surface: Something shrinking or sloping downward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decreasing' looks like getting smaller; split it as de-creasing, removing creases.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes are laid on this padded household stand while wrinkles are pressed out with a hot iron.

clue.text: Holiday house in Strasbourg I test

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words Strasbourg I test

explanation.surface: Someone trying out a holiday rental in the French city of Strasbourg.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a rural holiday cottage is common in British holiday brochures for self-catering lets.

clue.text: Felt these bats surrounding adult — they come out at night

indicators.note: surrounding says the scrambled letters close around the adult letter
bats means crazy, so the letters of felt these are scrambled

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Someone felt flying bats circling a grown-up after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals that come out at night; it is the anagram signal, turning FELT THESE into a mix around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are taken out of the mouth and soaked overnight, so they come out at bedtime.

clue.text: Party remains behind Boris, initially

indicators.note: behind places the remains after the letter from Boris
initially takes only the first letter of Boris

parts.note: the remains of a fire are ash

explanation.surface: A party loyalist lingering behind Boris Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is informal British slang for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Not pragmatic scholar

definitions.meaning: an adjective: theoretical, of no practical relevance
a noun: a university teacher or researcher

explanation.surface: An unworldly, impractical bookish person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both purely theoretical and a university lecturer or researcher.

clue.text: The man scoffed after model's delay

indicators.note: after places the scoffed letters following the model's

parts.note: the man is he
to model for an artist is to sit; the apostrophe-s is read as part of the leaf
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: A man ate up a model's time, holding things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back or pause before acting is to delay, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Rabbit in the sack?

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for chatter, and the sack is slang for bed: chatter in bed

explanation.surface: A bunny caught in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit (from rabbit and pork, rhyming slang) means talk; the sack is bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate conversation between lovers lying in bed is the idiom asked for.

clue.text: Dad's collecting new cooking equipment

indicators.note: collecting says the father's letters gather up the new letter inside them

parts.note: Dad is pa, so Dad's is pa's

explanation.surface: Father's kitchen gaining fresh pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucepans and frying pans are kitchen utensils; the plural matches equipment as a collective.

clue.text: These may prevent fighting if people space out, leaving line

indicators.note: space out means to spread around, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaving says the line letter departs from the words if people space

explanation.surface: Advice that giving each other room stops brawls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving line' removes L from IF PEOPLE SPACE; 'out' then shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Native American tradition shared a calumet or tobacco stem to seal truces, so these smoking implements mark an end to hostilities.

clue.text: Reach a temperature that isn't regularly dropping

indicators.note: dropping letters at regular intervals keeps every other letter of that isn't

explanation.surface: A thermometer reading that keeps falling instead of rising.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve or arrive at a goal is to reach it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Starts to reimburse everyone there if money's withdrawn

indicators.note: the starts of the four words are their first letters

parts.note: a cent is a coin, a unit of money

explanation.surface: An offer to repay everyone if their cash was taken out of the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' looks like money taken out of an account; it is the definition, meaning shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawn person is reserved and unwilling to speak, a synonym in character.

clue.text: Animal backbone? Not good guess

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, an animal

indicators.note: not says the good letter is absent from the backbone word

parts.note: backbone in the sense of courage or spirit is gumption

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a creature's spine is unsound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backbone' looks anatomical; it means spirit, GUMPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A supposition taken as true without proof is a guess, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Urges Cumberbatch, perhaps, to get food

parts.note: to egg on is to urge, so urges is eggs
Benedict Cumberbatch is a British actor; perhaps marks him as one example of the first name

explanation.surface: Someone pushing the actor Cumberbatch to grab a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Poached eggs on muffins with ham and hollandaise is a brunch dish, so it counts as a kind of food.

clue.text: Zulu and Bambi broadcast by western European country

parts.note: Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of Bambi are mixed

explanation.surface: A Zulu and the Disney deer shown on Western European television.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlocked southern African nation is a country, an example of the category.

clue.text: Upright position

definitions.meaning: an adjective: erect, on one's feet
a noun: status or reputation in society

explanation.surface: A vertical posture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both erect on one's feet and rank or reputation, as in good social status.

clue.text: Opening statement in court I don't fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters of court I don't are rearranged

explanation.surface: A litigant's opening remark in court, admitting they dislike the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' reads as a verb (I don't like); it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The preliminary part of a speech or book is its opening, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Burden women's rowing crew?

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
a racing boat with eight rowers, and the crew itself, is an eight

explanation.surface: A heavy load borne by a female rowing team.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy load or oppressive responsibility is a burden, a synonym.

clue.text: Swindled Conservative departs, furious

indicators.note: departs says the Conservative letter leaves the swindled word

parts.note: swindled means cheated

explanation.surface: A conned Tory storms off in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated row is angry and passionate, so the word means very angry.

clue.text: Lean right out of bed — time to reveal bust

parts.note: an aircraft leans or tilts when it banks
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Leaning over to get up, and time to show off one's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a chest; it is the slang adjective for insolvent.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that has gone bust is insolvent, unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: A slice each

parts.note: a slice of cake is a piece

explanation.surface: Cutting a portion for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Costing two pounds per item, for every one, is an adverb synonym for each.

clue.text: Continue abandoning area and cross river

indicators.note: abandoning says the area letter is dropped from the continue word

parts.note: to continue in a place is to stay
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: Pressing on, leaving a region and crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the dead are ferried across this underworld waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: This underworld waterway of Greek mythology is an example of a river.

clue.text: See red pimple

definitions.meaning: a verb phrase: to become very angry, seethe
a noun: an inflamed swelling on the skin

explanation.surface: Spotting a red spot on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to seethe with anger and a pus-filled skin swelling.

clue.text: Shaken drink going round is Tango

indicators.note: going round says the drink word encircles the other letters

parts.note: a draught is a swallow of drink
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cocktail shaken while the tango dance goes on around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shaken is upset and agitated, so the word is a synonym for deeply troubled.

clue.text: For that reason monster returns

indicators.note: returns means the monster word is read backwards

parts.note: an ogre is a monster

explanation.surface: Explaining why a monster comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word means therefore, used to draw a conclusion.

clue.text: Nude except pants? Not anticipated

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or poor, a sign that the letters of nude except are jumbled

explanation.surface: Naked apart from underwear: a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear; it is British slang for bad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not foreseen comes as a surprise, so the word is a synonym phrase.
